title: Spot the unsupported claims
scenario: A strategy briefing goes to your leadership team tomorrow. You have one pass to mark the claims that need evidence attached before the deck ships.
task: Flag every claim that should not be trusted as-is.
response:
Market update:

The sector grew 23% year over year. Three of the top five vendors will move to usage-based pricing by 2028. Customers increasingly expect transparent pricing. Our churn was 4.2% last quarter, according to our analytics dashboard. Experts agree the shift is inevitable. The competitor's pricing page lists three tiers.

claims.text: The sector grew 23% year over year.
claims.feedback: A precise statistic with no source — whose measurement, which segment, which year? Attach evidence or replace it with a sourced direction.

claims.text: Three of the top five vendors will move to usage-based pricing by 2028.
claims.feedback: A prediction with a count and a date, stated as fact. Nobody knows this; label it as a scenario or find the analyst report behind it.
Qualitative and directional — nothing checkable enough to be factually wrong. Just make sure no number gets attached later.

claims.text: Our churn was 4.2% last quarter, according to our analytics dashboard.
claims.feedback: It names its source and you can open it. Verify the dashboard figure, but the claim itself points at its evidence.

claims.text: Experts agree the shift is inevitable.
claims.feedback: Anonymous authority plus absolutism — which experts, agreeing on what? A claim that names nothing cannot be checked.

claims.text: The competitor's pricing page lists three tiers.
claims.feedback: Specific, but checkable in one click at a named place. Confirm the page, then it is safe.

hints: Scan for digits, dates and 'experts' — each one needs a source or a label.
One statement names where to find its own evidence. Is that a problem?
explanation: The flagged claims carry specifics — a percentage, a dated prediction, an unnamed authority — with nothing to check them against. The others assert nothing measurable, name their source, or point at a page you can open. Specificity plus consequence plus no evidence equals the danger zone.
